findings.excerpt: theorem coe_basis_apply (r : ι) : (basis j X i e he hrepr hfix r : CartierModule p X.F) = e r := by
findings.problem: The simp chain is only half-set-up. `coe_eSub` is tagged `@[scoped simp]`, but `basis_apply` and `coe_basis_apply` are plain theorems. `basis_apply` is the step that turns `basis ... r` into `eSub ... r`. The canonical, user-facing form is the coercion `(basis ... r : CartierModule p X.F) = e r`, and that is `coe_basis_apply`. This lemma has no simp attribute either. So `simp` cannot normalise `↑(basis j X i e he hrepr hfix r)` to `e r`. Callers must `rw [coe_basis_apply] at h'` by hand, as at line 211, and again when assembling `solution`. The sibling definitions file marks its analogous coercion-of-application lemmas `@[simp]`, for example `coe_endODInvariants_apply`.
findings.proposed_change: Mark `coe_basis_apply` `@[scoped simp]`, to match `coe_eSub`. Mark `basis_apply` `@[scoped simp]` too if the intermediate `eSub` form should be reachable. Both are oriented towards the simpler term. Every argument of the left-hand side appears in the pattern, so no hypothesis side goals arise. The `injective_endMatrix` proof could then use `simpa using h'` instead of `rwa [coe_basis_apply] at h'`.
findings.benefit: Users who open `R4E1Inj` get a consistent normal form, where the coercion of the chosen basis vector reduces to the given frame vector `e r`. They don't need to remember a manual rewrite. The simp set also becomes consistent between `eSub` and `basis`.
